text:
incident-bot: PAGER: latency SLO breach detected in shared-gpu-pool (p99 > 5s for generation endpoint) — auto-created incident. Please acknowledge with /ack. :rotating_light:

maya (oncall): acked. seeing alerts for gen-v2 and streaming stalls on 3 nodes in us-west-2. p95 ~ 1.2s but p99 spikes to 6-12s. important: this is multi-tenant cluster (shared-gpu-pool).

ryan: dumping recent tail logs and sched traces now. looks like heavy IO wait + gpu stalls around 2026-03-14T18:00Z. attaching quick output: 
```\n# iostat -x 1 3\nDevice:         rrqm/s wrqm/s   r/s   w/s  rsec/s  wsec/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svpct\nnvme0n1         0.00   10.00  0.50 120.00  10.00  4800.00 40.0     1.20    9.8   0.3    12.0   99.0\n```\n\nekaterina: :eyes: those avgqu-sz numbers are concerning — possible NVMe saturation from another tenant. can we check cgroup blkio/weight + per-container IO stats?

eng-runtime: we have a recent change that loosened cgroup blkio throttling for bursty workloads (to reduce stalls), might be backfiring when multiple heavy jobs overlap. checking kernel throttling counters.

maya (oncall): running ps + nvidia-smi on affected nodes: `ssh node-07 'nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,used_memory,sm_util --format=csv'`. results: two tenant containers showing 98% SM util, others show stalled kernels.

ryan: also seeing cgroup cpu throttling spikes: `cat /sys/fs/cgroup/cpuacct/docker/<id>/cpu.stat` shows high nr_periods and nr_throttled. possible noisy neighbor.

sre-shift: can we identify which tenants? I can cordon node-07 and migrate low-priority pods while we triage. prefer to avoid full drain if customers affected.

customer-success: pinging to get impacted customer list. preliminary: 4 customers showing elevated API latencies; two are on public plan (fallback to hosted) and two are on dedicated tenants but routed through shared pool for some workloads. I'll update customers.

maya (oncall): quick mitigation plan proposals: 1) enable temporary stricter blkio throttling for noisy containers, 2) move heavy batch jobs to dedicated reserved pool (if capacity), 3) if immediate relief needed, cordon affected nodes and failover streaming sessions to other regions. thoughts?

ekaterina: do 1 + 2 first. blkio throttle via `echo "<major>:<minor> <io_bps>" > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/docker/<id>/blkio.throttle.write_bps_device` — but this is invasive. can ops-bot apply a safelist script to identify top writers and apply a soft throttle?

ops-bot: Running identification script (top_io.sh) on node-07... found container ids: ctnr-a1b2 (tenant: data-analytics), ctnr-c3d4 (tenant: image-batch). Top write bytes/sec: 120MB/s and 95MB/s respectively.

eng-runtime: recommend setting per-tenant throttle to 50MB/s for a 10m window and monitor. I'll prepare a rollback command.

maya (oncall): proceeding with soft throttle on ctnr-a1b2 and ctnr-c3d4. executing: 
```\necho "8:0 52428800" > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/docker/ctnr-a1b2/blkio.throttle.write_bps_device\necho "8:0 52428800" > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/docker/ctnr-c3d4/blkio.throttle.write_bps_device\n```\n\nops-bot: Applied blkio throttle to ctnr-a1b2 and ctnr-c3d4. Will auto-revert in 10m unless extended.

ryan: watching metrics — p99 dropped from ~9.8s to ~3.2s within 60s. streaming stalls reduced, but still occasional 2-3s stalls.

customer-success: update: customer alpha (id: cust-425) reporting partial degradation but they've acknowledged mitigation and asked for ETA on full recovery.

eng-runtime: noticed a config drift in cgroup weights: `systemctl show --property=Environment inference-runtime` had BLKIO_WEIGHT unset on some nodes after recent rollout. rolling out a patch to set conservative BLKIO_WEIGHT=300 across shared pool.

sre-shift: cordoned node-09 as precaution (suspect similar pattern). migrating 8 low-priority pods to cold pool. will keep node-07 online for now to avoid mass reconnect churn.

maya (oncall): setting severity P1 -> P2? This is affecting production but mitigation is in place and p99 back to ~1.5-2.5s now. Thoughts?

eng-runtime: recommend P2 for now. we should still run a root cause investigation: likely noisy neighbor causing NVMe queue saturation + weakened blkio cgroup settings from a recent change.

ekaterina: capturing runbook steps and commands used in the incident doc. will include reproduction checklist and recommended permanent fixes: enforce BLKIO_WEIGHT baseline, limit batch job write_bps, and provide autoscaler to move heavy batch jobs to reserved pool automatically.

ops-bot: audit event created: audit-evt-1840001234-01 — actions: blkio-throttle-applied (ctnr-a1b2, ctnr-c3d4), node-cordon (node-09), node-migrate (8 pods).

maya (oncall): handing incident to ryan for night support. summary for handoff: "P99 latency spike caused by NVMe saturation from two heavy tenants. Immediate mitigation: soft blkio throttle applied to top writers (50MB/s) and cordon of one suspicious node. p99 down to ~1.8s. Follow-ups: enforce BLKIO_WEIGHT baseline across pool, add per-tenant burst tokens or move batch jobs to reserved pools, postmortem and customer communications."

ryan: taking over oncall. I have checkpointed logs and a timeline. will open a postmortem ticket and schedule post-incident review with eng-runtime + SRE.

customer-success: sending customer communication drafts to legal and SRE for review. will include affected times, mitigation steps, and follow-up actions. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident status updated to INVESTIGATING -> MITIGATED at 1840001298. Owner: ryan.

maya (oncall): final note — we should add a streaming-tail test that simulates concurrent heavy writers to shared NVMe to catch regressions. adding to backlog. :memo:
